clue.text: Wise man conceals women's article in Dorset

definitions.note: a place in Dorset: the answer is a town there

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so the wise man wraps around the next letters

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
W is the standard abbreviation for women
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A learned man hides a piece of women's clothing somewhere in Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests clothing after 'women's', but it is the grammatical article AN. SWANAGE is a seaside town on the Dorset coast in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanage is a resort town located on the Purbeck coast of that English county.

clue.text: Cooking utensil for butcher in film scene

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the butcher word goes within the film word

parts.note: a film scene is shot on a set
to butcher is to kill

explanation.surface: A frying pan used as a prop for a slaughter scene in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan or small heavy pan used on the stove.

clue.text: Doctor gripped by dread in the middle of …

indicators.note: something gripped by another is held inside it, so the doctor sits within the dread

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
MO is Medical Officer, a common crossword doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is seized with dread halfway through something, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface only; each is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst is a preposition meaning surrounded by or among, which is being placed centrally among others.

clue.text: … inspection of car (make and model)

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A check-up of a car, with the make and model noted in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a form to fill in, but it asks for a car make and then a car model.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of accounts or records, a formal inspection.

clue.text: A couple of space travellers discover fungus

parts.note: the first of the pair: our planet travels through space round the sun
the second of the pair: a star also moves through space

explanation.surface: Two astronauts come across a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space travellers' suggests astronauts, but here they are heavenly bodies that move through space.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthstar is a puffball fungus whose outer skin splits into a star shape on the ground.

clue.text: Tries round about 0.001" in this sort of graph

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tries word goes around the measurement
to turn round is to face the other way, so the word for tries is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a try, so goes are tries
a mil is a thousandth of an inch

explanation.surface: Plotting attempts at around a thousandth of an inch on a particular kind of graph.
explanation.walkthrough: The inch mark is the clue's own symbol; one-thousandth of an inch is a mil in engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A semilog graph has one axis on a logarithmic scale and the other linear, a recognised type of chart.

clue.text: Expensive marinade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... price is a high one
second meaning: to soak food in liquid

explanation.surface: A costly sauce for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for overpriced and is also a verb meaning to soak something in liquid, as one marinades food.

clue.text: Man sheltering god's draught animal

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the man word encloses the god word

parts.note: a man is a male
Thor is the Norse god of thunder, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A man gives cover to a deity's carthorse.
explanation.walkthrough: A malt-horse, a heavy horse used to grind malt, is an old word Shakespeare uses as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A malthorse was a heavy horse used to turn the brewer's malt mill, so a working beast of burden.

clue.text: On a low hill, stages entertainment

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the stages come first and the hill follows

parts.note: legs are stages of a journey or race
a how is a dialect word for a low hill or mound, as in northern English place names

explanation.surface: Performances put on from a small rise in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stages' looks like a verb meaning puts on a show, but it is a noun here. The definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-show is a theatrical revue featuring dancers who display their legs, a type of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Lightweight's hurt in this sort of school

parts.note: a gram is a tiny unit of weight
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A small boxer gets injured at a certain kind of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight' suggests a boxer but means a small unit of weight; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar school is a selective British secondary school that admits pupils by examination.

clue.text: Properly arranged so as not to …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tidy, in the correct sequence
second meaning: with the purpose, as in 'so as not to' meaning the same as the phrase followed by 'not to'

explanation.surface: Things set out neatly to avoid upsetting someone, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'not to' complete the phrase in the surface and run on into the next clue; they are not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means correctly sequenced or tidy, and also introduces a purpose, as a substitute for the conjunction 'so as'.

clue.text: … disconcert goalie with universal encomia

indicators.note: to disconcert someone is to throw them into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: Fulsome praise could put a goalkeeper off his game.
explanation.walkthrough: Encomia is the plural of encomium, high praise; the answer is the plural of eulogium.
explanation.definitionFit: Eulogia are formal speeches or writings of praise, just as encomia are tributes of high praise.

clue.text: Delicate, small and up-to-date navigational warning

parts.note: light means delicate, as of a touch
S is the abbreviation for small
hip means fashionable, up to date

explanation.surface: A dainty, fashionable little alert for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel with a beacon that warns ships of hazards, serving as a floating lighthouse.

clue.text: Dull house has bad smell

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
hum is British slang for a stink

explanation.surface: A boring home with a nasty whiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho-hum describes something boring and unremarkable, the sound of a weary yawn.

clue.text: Colossus represented by half-hearted artist

indicators.note: only half the heart is kept, so of the two central letters one is dropped

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A giant statue rendered by an artist who lacked enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the painter's name is its middle pair of letters, II; half of that is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size or power, as a colossus is a giant.

clue.text: What H. King designed for flier

indicators.note: something designed is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what some H. King drew up for a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nighthawk is an American bird related to the nightjar, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: People of the highest stand-ing execute artist

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them
one who draws is an artist

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk put a painter to death.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'stand-ing' hints that a stand, a piece of furniture, is involved: a top drawer is the highest part of a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest social class or quality, so it describes the elite.

clue.text: Mineral disturbed antelopes

indicators.note: things disturbed are moved out of place, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some rock has upset a herd of antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleonaste is a dark green to black variety of spinel, which is a mineral.

clue.text: People coming to Silver Lake for a show of animals

parts.note: men are people
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Visitors travel to Silver Lake to watch an animal display.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition to the public.

clue.text: Sailor gives lashings in support of ship's officer

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so the lashings piece is placed below the officer

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
lashings means plenty, a lot

explanation.surface: A seaman whips the crew to back up a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashings' suggests flogging, but it is British slang for lots of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is informal British slang, borrowed from French, for a sailor in the navy.

clue.text: Lauren Bacall's initial broadcast concerning a group of stars

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter, so only the start of the surname is used

parts.note: the first letter of the actress's surname

explanation.surface: A radio piece about the film star Lauren Bacall and the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: The full first name is used but only the initial of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebular is the adjective from nebula, a cloud of gas or a cluster of stars in space.

clue.text: Park in former elevated railway and drive out

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the park letter goes inside the following pair

parts.note: ex means former
the El is the American name for an elevated railway, as in Chicago
P is the abbreviation for park or parking

explanation.surface: Parking at a disused overhead railway, then driving off.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone or something to leave, to eject or banish.

clue.text: F1 champion entertained very old college head

indicators.note: a host who entertains guests has them inside, so the champion holds the next letters

parts.note: Alain Prost was four times Formula One world champion
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A racing champion hosts an elderly head of college.
explanation.definitionFit: A provost is the head of certain colleges at Oxford, Cambridge and elsewhere.

clue.text: Many a breadwinner is an apprentice

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
a breadwinner earns the family's income

explanation.surface: Plenty of family providers are trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' standing for a Roman numeral such as L or C is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone still being taught a trade or skill, like an apprentice.

clue.text: Land punt after it's come back

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it, so the bet comes second
coming back means going the opposite way, so the word it is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written, with the 's read as 'has'
a punt is a gamble or bet

explanation.surface: A boat comes ashore after returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' looks like a flat-bottomed boat but means a wager; the 's in 'it's' is read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a region and country on the high plateau north of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Frenchman injured Estonian in America

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman hurt a Baltic visitor somewhere in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a state in the northern Midwest of the USA, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Starts to make all disciples look yonder with ardour

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each following word contributes only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Something moves every follower to gaze into the distance passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Madly means with wild passion or intensity, as in loving someone madly.

clue.text: Type of nest that's unknown in lake

indicators.note: a thing in another is enclosed by it, so the unknown goes inside the lake

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious kind of nest found in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters such as X, Y and Z stand for unknowns, as in algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built high on a crag.

clue.text: Everybody returned to interrupt noble heretic

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this piece goes inside the noble

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for everybody is read from the end

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: The whole crowd came back to break in on a nobleman who was a dissenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lollard was a follower of John Wycliffe in medieval England, condemned by the Church as a heretic.

clue.text: Redhead in store gets popular cut of meat

indicators.note: a thing in another is placed inside it, so the selected letter goes within the store

parts.note: a silo is a store for grain
the head of the word red is its first letter
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person in a shop buys a favourite joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' suggests a person with red hair but splits into red and head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is the choice joint of beef from the upper loin, a prized cut.

clue.text: Jailer and knight tucking into Christmas fare

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the knight letter is placed within the Christmas fare

parts.note: turkey is the traditional Christmas meal
N is the chess notation for a knight, since K is taken by the king

explanation.surface: A prison warder and a knight are eating Christmas dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but it means slipping inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a jailer, the one who holds and turns the keys of the cells.

clue.text: Horse rider always covers slit in jacket

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap over it, so the always word goes around the slit

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a vent is a slit in the back or side of a jacket

explanation.surface: A rider's jacket always has a slit at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er, the poetic short form of ever, is a common crossword way to clue always.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider competing in eventing, the combined equestrian contest of dressage, cross-country and jumping.
